newsitem.title: POLAND: BRE eyes investment, private banking rise.
newsitem.headline: BRE eyes investment, private banking rise.

text.p: Poland's Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA (BRE), marking its 10th anniversary, wants to focus its strategy on the expansion of its investment banking and private banking services, the bank's president said on Tuesday.

Krzysztof Szwarc told a news conference the bank, which had secured a leading position in corporate banking and trade finance by implementing cutting-edge electronic systems, planned to expand beyond its core client-base.

"Our main client-base right now are large and medium-sized firms with annual sales of at least $5 million but we plan to pay more attention to smaller companies with high growth potential," Szwarc said.
Szwarc also said BRE, 21-percent owned by Germany's Commerzbank AG, was expanding its investment banking operations.

"Our new strategy also entails development of investment banking activities...and we are already visible on the market because of our commercial paper programmes and underwriting activities," Szwarc said.
He also said the bank was also fast developing its private banking services for affluent individuals who can deposit at least 100,000 zlotys.
"We need to find a market niche. We won't be expanding into retail banking but certainly private banking is one of the areas we want to expand," Szwarc told reporters after the conference.

He said that so far profits growth was sufficient to keep the bank's capital rising in line with its balance sheet growth and if the trend continued the bank would not need new share issues until 1998.
Asked whether its strategic partner Commerzbank would seek to up its stake Szwarc said:
"I would not be surprised if at some point Commerzbank decided to increase its share but so far I am not aware of such plans."
BRE is Poland's 15th largest bank in terms of assets, accounting for around 1.5 percent of total assets in the Polish banking system.
BRE's balance sheet total at the end of 1995 was 2.58 billion zlotys and its capital 317 million zlotys.
The bank had a net profit of 68.1 million zlotys in the first half of 1996, up from 49.3 million in the first half of 1995.
